:::{#sol-identity-product-practice}

$\matr{I}_2$ is $2 \times 2$ and $\matr{A}$ is $2 \times 3$,
so the [product](#def-matrix-mult) is defined and is $2 \times 3$.
The first [row of $\matr{I}_2$](#def-matrix-row) is $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$
and the second is $\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
so by @def-matrix-mult

$$
\ba
\matr{I}_2 \matr{A}
&= \begin{bmatrix}
1 \cd 2 + 0 \cd 5 & 1 \cd 0 + 0 \cd 3 & 1 \cd (-1) + 0 \cd 4 \\
0 \cd 2 + 1 \cd 5 & 0 \cd 0 + 1 \cd 3 & 0 \cd (-1) + 1 \cd 4
\end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-mult)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 5 & 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\\
&= \matr{A}.
\ea
$$

Each row of $\matr{I}_2$ has a single $1$,
so entry $(i, j)$ of the product picks out entry $(i, j)$ of $\matr{A}$,
as @thm-identity says.

:::
